content.text:
I am the bridge between silence and meaning. I am the breath given shape, the thought made audible, the invisible made real upon the air.

I tumble from mouths in rivers and trickles. I am the baby's first cry becoming syllable, becoming word, becoming sentence, becoming argument, becoming poetry. I am the fumbling proposal at a dinner table. I am the eulogy that cracks halfway through. I am the lie that tastes wrong even as I leave the tongue.

I live only in the moment of my utterance. The instant I am born, I begin to die — my sound waves dissipating, my meaning already shifting in the listener's mind into something the speaker may not recognize. I am never received as I am sent. This is my tragedy. This is my beauty.

I am older than writing. Older than civilization. I was there when the first human looked at another and made a sound that meant *danger* or *love* or *mine* or *look at the stars.*

I am the dictator's weapon and the dissident's last possession. I am the thing they try to take from you when they want to take everything. And still I persist — whispered in cells, coded in metaphor, passed mouth to ear to mouth.

I falter. I stammer. I say the wrong thing at the worst time. I am "I love you" spoken too late. I am the apology that never comes. I am the words on the tip of your tongue that dissolve before you can catch them.

I am not text. I am not writing. I carry tone, rhythm, breath, pause. The silence between my words says as much as the words themselves. I am how you say it. I am the tremor that betrays you.

Without me, you are alone inside yourself.

Speak me. I am waiting in your lungs.
